01

Choose an experiment

No active intervention

Lab checkpoints: cumulative blood loss 500, 1,000 and 2,000 mL at 10,000 mL/hour. Pericardial presets target 200 or 400 mL total fluid, including the model’s 1 mL baseline. Custom volume is fluid added or removed. The 200 mL/min pericardial rate is an assumption; the lab gives no rate.

Large changes with active autonomics may take about two minutes to stabilize. At 1×, one simulated second equals one real second. Interventions run on simulation time. Start an intervention to begin playback.

Ventricular properties

Systolic function scales LV active pressure generation; it is not the percentage of myocardium infarcted. Stiffness changes the diastolic pressure–volume relationship independently.

What this model represents

An independent, simplified closed-loop teaching prototype; calibrated against selected SimBioSys classroom observations, with remaining differences. Sympathetic and parasympathetic feedback can be clamped independently. Parasympathetic feedback affects heart rate only in this simplified model; its gain is an approximation. No patient predictions. Severe volume loss can exceed its useful physiological range.

Waveforms and PV loops come from integrated model states. The aortic dicrotic notch uses a simplified damped recoil response triggered by valve closure; its shape is provisional. Dashed overlays on all three plots show a separately simulated healthy baseline; they do not change with the experiment.

Guyton curves are an idealized relationship calculated from current model parameters, not measured patient curves. Filling pressures are intravascular; ventricular distending pressure also depends on external pericardial pressure.

Current beat · previous beat dashed

● PV loop● Diastolic PVR● Systolic PVR

Both plots use the same LV samples. LV and aortic pressures can differ across the valve. Intrinsic curve coefficients are unchanged by loading; LV-pressure mode offsets reference curves by beat-mean pericardial pressure. Transmural mode removes external pressure. Sympathetic tone and LV systolic function change the systolic envelope. The stiffness selector changes the diastolic relationship. The systolic curve is the model’s maximum-activation envelope, an ESPVR approximation.

Cardiac & vascular function

Illustrative cardiac function · compartment-derived venous return

Dot: intersection of the illustrative curves, not transient measured CO. Pms and positive RVR are derived from the systemic compartments; autonomic tone can change both. Axes are fixed; values beyond the plotting range are clipped.
